chapter: After the road: New York, the profession and advice
title: Summing up his career and passing knowledge on
summary: Hinton sums up Jackson's career from the Buckeye Melodians to the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band; both say passing knowledge on is a kind of immortality.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: We've been speaking with Quentin Jackson, one of the finest gentlemen in all the band business. He has played for all of the greatest musicians in the world, with the greatest bands, with the greatest orchestras, beginning with -- What was the first, beginning, Butter? Who was the first band?
The first band that I -- the Buckeye Melodians at home to Wesley Helvey's Troubadours to Zack White, and my first big name band, McKinney Cotton Pickers.

McKinney Cotton Pickers, all the way consistently, consistently playing trombone and singing through all of this to right now, here today, the Mel Lewis-Thad Jones band. If you can tell me in this year of 1976 of anybody that can compare with this, I'm willing to listen. Butter, I want to thank you. Quentin Jackson, I want to thank you. I want to thank your lovely wife which we didn't get a chance to talk too much about but which has been such a strong influence and helping you in your life, --
Uh-huh.
-- and we wish you continued health and success. And we know you've been through a tremendous amount of things with health problems but, thanks to heaven,
you're cool again and playing.
Oh, yes, I'm always going to play.
Beautiful.
And I hope, if I can, I will help some kids along the best I can, you know. I'm always willing to help because someone helped me, --
That's the story. That's the my exact feelings
Butter.
-- you see, and it should be passed on.
It should be. That's my idea of what immortality is.
Uh-huh.
If I can pass on whatever I've learned in my way along this world to someone else, then that means that I'll never really be gone, --
Uh-huh.
-- because whatever I've learned I passed on.
Uh-huh.
And when they go if they will pass it on, this is my assurance of immortality.
That's right, that's right.
